from.place: Proof paragraph 2, the coherent Hom comparison: the universal left fibration over the space quasicategory is the unstraightening of the identity, so pulling it back along a space-valued functor realizes that functor.

title: Universal left fibration represents the identity on spaces
statement:
Use quasicategories, spaces, internal functor simplicial sets and coherent equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], left fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and the coherent nerve of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal V$, let $\operatorname{Kan}_{\mathcal U}$ be the simplicial category of $\mathcal U$-small Kan complexes with their simplicial mapping complexes, and put $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\operatorname{Kan}_{\mathcal U})$. Constructions involving this whole category are performed in a containing universe. Define
$$W=\{\Delta^0\}\times_{\mathcal S_{\mathcal U},\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}),\qquad r=\operatorname{ev}_1:W\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}.$$
For a base $B$, normalize covariant classification by the right-derived ordinary functor $U^{\mathrm{cov}}_B$ of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation] and the enriched-evaluation comparison of [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-rectification]: a coherent diagram is represented by a projectively cofibrant-fibrant strict diagram, to which one applies the ordinary functor $U^{\mathrm{cov}}_B$. Then $r$ is a left fibration classified by $\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}}$ under this normalization. For every quasicategory $B$ and coherent functor $F:B\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$, its degreewise pullback $F^*W\to B$ represents $F$ under the same classification. The comparison is natural in $F$ and in maps of bases. In particular, its fiber at $b$ is equivalent to $F(b)$, and pullback along $u:B'\to B$ represents $F\circ u$.

source.place: HTT Section 3.3.2 (Universal Fibrations), Definition 3.3.2.2, Proposition 3.3.2.6 and Corollaries 3.3.2.7–8 (printed pp.210–213): restrict the universal Cartesian fibration to spaces and dualize; its slice model is represented by the terminal space. The fixed-source arrow model is equivalent to the join coslice (dual of lem-coef-infinity-slice-arrow-equivalence). The normalization uses Section 2.2.1 and Proposition 4.2.4.4. Read online, not archived; archival source WANTED. No Stacks tag.

proof.text: Write $A=\operatorname{Kan}_{\mathcal U}$, $S=N_{\mathrm{hc}}A$, and $e=\Delta^0\in A$. Work in a universe large enough to contain $A$, $S$, and any base under consideration; the Kan model category used for rectification is the category of simplicial sets in that containing universe. Its cofibrations are monomorphisms by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], so all its objects are cofibrant, and it is combinatorial and simplicial by [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model]. The simplicial model axiom of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] applied to $\varnothing\to K$ and $L\to *$ shows that $\operatorname{Fun}(K,L)$ is Kan when $L$ is Kan. Thus $A$ is locally Kan and $S$ is a quasicategory by [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Let $\epsilon:\mathfrak C[S]\to A$ be the coherent-nerve counit and define the strict covariant diagram $h(x)=A(e,\epsilon x)$. Evaluation gives an isomorphism $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^0,K)\cong K$: in degree $n$ it sends a map $\Delta^0\times\Delta^n\to K$ to the corresponding $n$-simplex. Postcomposition respects this isomorphism in every simplicial degree. Use this natural isomorphism to identify $h$ with the composite of $\epsilon$ and the inclusion of $A$ into simplicial sets. If $\eta_S:S\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathfrak C[S]$ is the unit, the adjunction identity $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\epsilon)\eta_S=1_S$ shows that enriched evaluation of $h$ gives the identity of $S$, followed by the inclusion into the ambient space category. This inclusion retains exactly the same mapping simplicial sets on $\mathcal U$-small Kan complexes; no change of the space-valued diagram is being made.

source.place: Sections 1.1.5 and 2.2.1; Proposition 4.2.4.4. Explicit evaluation-at-a-point calculation.

proof.text: Compute $U^{\mathrm{cov}}_S h$ using the formula of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation], rather than inferring a classifier from its fibers. Identify $\mathfrak C[S^{\mathrm{op}}]$ with $\mathfrak C[S]^{\mathrm{op}}$ by reversal of vertex labels, and use $\epsilon^{\mathrm{op}}$ as a functor to $A^{\mathrm{op}}$. For a simplex $\sigma:\Delta^n\to S^{\mathrm{op}}$, put $M_\sigma=\mathfrak C[\Delta^n\star\Delta^0]\amalg_{\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]}\mathfrak C[S^{\mathrm{op}}]$ and let $v$ be its cone vertex. An enriched natural map $T_\sigma\to h$ is precisely an enriched functor $M_\sigma\to A^{\mathrm{op}}$ extending $\epsilon^{\mathrm{op}}$ and sending $v$ to $e$: its maps on the old-to-$v$ mapping sets are the components $M_\sigma(x,v)\to A^{\mathrm{op}}(\epsilon x,e)=A(e,\epsilon x)$ of the natural map. There are no maps from $v$ to an old object, the identity at $v$ is forced, and the remaining composition equations are exactly enriched naturality. The pushout property makes this the same data as a functor $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n\star\Delta^0]\to A^{\mathrm{op}}$ extending $\epsilon^{\mathrm{op}}\mathfrak C[\sigma]$ with final object $e$. By the nerve adjunction in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], these are exactly the $(n+1)$-simplices of $S^{\mathrm{op}}$ with initial face $\sigma$ and last vertex $e$. Here $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(A^{\mathrm{op}})=(N_{\mathrm{hc}}A)^{\mathrm{op}}$ follows directly by reversing the subset labels in the stated thickening; union composition is preserved. Both directions of this bijection restrict by precomposition with every simplex operator. Hence $U_{S^{\mathrm{op}}}h\cong(S^{\mathrm{op}})_{/e}$ over $S^{\mathrm{op}}$. Taking opposites as required by the specified normalization gives an isomorphism $p:U^{\mathrm{cov}}_S h\cong S_{e/}$ over $S$, where an $n$-simplex on the right is a map $\Delta^0\star\Delta^n\to S$ with first vertex $e$. The slice convention is that of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration], dualized.

source.place: Section 2.2.1, cone definition of straightening and its right adjoint; Section 3.3.2, terminal-space representability. Explicit adjunction and pushout calculation.

proof.text: The diagram $h$ is objectwise Kan. In its projective model structure factor $\varnothing\to h$ as a cofibration followed by a trivial fibration $Qh\to h$, using the functorial factorization of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. Then $Qh$ is cofibrant and fibrant, since $Qh\to h\to *$ is a fibration. By [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation], both $U^{\mathrm{cov}}_S Qh$ and $U^{\mathrm{cov}}_S h$ are left fibrations and the induced map between them is an equivalence over $S$. Rectification [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-rectification] applies with $K=S$, $\mathcal C=\mathfrak C[S]$, $u=1$, and the ambient Kan model category, whose required combinatorial simplicial structure is supplied by [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model]. Its comparison is induced by enriched evaluation. The enriched natural map $Qh\to h$ gives a coherent transformation from that evaluated diagram to $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(h)\eta_S$; each component is a weak equivalence between Kan complexes, hence an equivalence of spaces by [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] this transformation is an equivalence. Step 1 identifies its target with the identity diagram. Therefore the right-derived ordinary functor prescribed in the question represents the identity by $p:S_{e/}\to S$. Its fiber equivalences have essentially $\mathcal U$-small values, so this says identity on $S_{\mathcal U}$, with the containing universe used only to carry out replacements.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.1.2 and Proposition 4.2.4.4; explicit cofibrant replacement and evaluation comparison.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-target-right-fibration] to $S^{\mathrm{op}}$ and the vertex $e$, and then reverse all simplices. A right horn with missing face $j>0$ becomes a left horn with missing face $n-j<n$. Reversing the interval interchanges its endpoints. The resulting left fibration is exactly $r:W\to S$ in the statement. Dualize [lem-coef-infinity-slice-arrow-equivalence] at the same vertex to get an equivalence $\delta:S_{e/}\to W$ over $S$. Explicitly it sends a cone simplex $\tau:\Delta^{n+1}\to S$ to its composite with the nerve of $[n]\times[1]\to[n+1]$, $(a,0)\mapsto0$, $(a,1)\mapsto a+1$. Restriction at the second endpoint is the base simplex, so the equation over $S$ holds strictly. Applying [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-fibers] to $\delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ shows that it is an equivalence on vertex fibers. The fiber criterion of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation] now makes $\delta$ a simplicial homotopy equivalence over $S$. Thus the arrow model and the normalized representative of step 3 represent the same identity diagram. In particular, this passage between models uses a map over the base, not merely unrelated equivalences of fibers.

source.place: Corollary 4.6.4.20 (02VT), Construction 4.6.4.15 (02GH), Proposition 4.6.4.13 (01KQ), and Corollary 4.5.3.31 (01HK); these are Kerodon tags, not Stacks tags.

proof.text: For $F:B\to S$ put $h_F=h\circ\mathfrak C[F]$. The base-change isomorphism of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation] gives $F^*p\cong U^{\mathrm{cov}}_B h_F$. All these are left fibrations: lifting against a horn in a pullback is lifting the corresponding horn against the original projection. Choose a projective cofibrant replacement $Qh_F\to h_F$ by trivial fibration as in step 3; it is again objectwise Kan. Rectification [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-rectification] with $K=B$, $\mathcal C=\mathfrak C[B]$, $u=1$ sends $Qh_F$ to its evaluated coherent diagram. The enriched natural map $Qh_F\to h_F$ induces a coherent transformation from that diagram to $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(h_F)\eta_B$. Its components are the objectwise weak equivalences $Qh_F(b)\to h_F(b)$ between Kan complexes. Naturality of the unit and step 1 give $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(h_F)\eta_B=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(h)\eta_S F=F$, interpreted in the ambient space category. The pointwise equivalence criterion [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] applies to $Qh_F\to h_F$ exactly as in step 3; weak equivalences are inverted by [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. Thus $F^*p$ represents $F$ in the fixed normalization. Pull back $\delta$ and its inverse and homotopies from step 4; pullback is degreewise and $F^*(X\times\Delta^1)=F^*X\times\Delta^1$ for a homotopy over $S$. Hence $F^*\delta:F^*p\to F^*W$ is a homotopy equivalence over $B$. It follows that $F^*W$ represents $F$. The fiber clause of the presentation gives $(F^*p)_b\simeq h_F(b)=F(b)$, and the pulled-back $\delta$ gives the same assertion for $F^*W$, including empty values.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.1.1 (base-change isomorphisms), Theorem 2.2.1.2 and Proposition 4.2.4.4; Corollary 3.3.2.8 for the universal-family interpretation.

proof.text: For any simplicial map $G:C\to S$, put $h_G=h\mathfrak C[G]$. It is objectwise Kan by step 1. By [lem-coef-kan-diagram-localized-evaluation], evaluating a projectively cofibrant-fibrant replacement $Qh_G\to h_G$ gives an equivalence of whole $C$-diagrams. The comparisons are independent of replacement and coherently compatible with restriction by [lem-coef-kan-diagram-evaluation-restriction]. Naturality of the adjunction unit gives $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(h_G)\eta_C=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(h)\eta_S G=G$ by step 1. The presentation base-change formula identifies $G^*p$ with $U^{\mathrm{cov}}_C h_G$, and preservation of the replacement weak equivalence identifies this with the normalized representative $U^{\mathrm{cov}}_C Qh_G$. The cited lemmas allow arbitrary simplicial $C$, including $B\times\Delta^n$.

source.place: HTT Propositions 2.2.1.1 and 4.2.4.4; whole-diagram evaluation and its restriction/replacement coherence are isolated in the two new general lemmas.

proof.text: For an $n$-simplex of $\operatorname{Fun}(B,S)$ take its adjoint $G:C=B\times\Delta^n\to S$ as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Step 6 gives its normalized representative on all of $C$. Its comparison to $G^*W$ is $G^*\delta$, following the cone identification of step 2 and the equivalence of step 4. If $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, restriction along $1_B\times\Delta(\alpha)$ carries this map to $(G(1_B\times\Delta(\alpha)))^*\delta$: in each degree both maps send a pullback pair $(c,x)$ to $(c,\delta(x))$. The cone bijection of step 2 also restricts by the same simplex map. The restriction coherence in [lem-coef-kan-diagram-evaluation-restriction] identifies the replacement/evaluation comparisons on these shapes. Hence the comparison is compatible with every higher simplex in $F$, not only its vertices.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.4.4; explicit simplex-parameter restriction of the comparison map, with replacement coherence supplied by the extracted lemma.

proof.text: For a base map $u:B'\to B$, the composition-compatible base-change isomorphisms of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation] give $u^*U^{\mathrm{cov}}_B h_F\cong U^{\mathrm{cov}}_{B'}(h_F\mathfrak C[u])=U^{\mathrm{cov}}_{B'}h_{Fu}$. For the arrow model, flattening a pullback triple gives $u^*(F^*W)\cong(Fu)^*W$, carrying $(b',(b,w))$ to $(b',w)$, where $b=u(b')$. Both comparison maps send $w$ to $\delta(w)$, so flattening commutes with them. The same equality holds after a parameter product with $\Delta^n$. Together with steps 6 and 7, this proves joint naturality in $F$ and base maps, and that pullback along $u$ represents $F\circ u$.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.1.1; explicit flattening of iterated pullback triples and its compatibility with the parameterized comparison.

lean.note: Uses the existing smallSpaces, transportSpaces and fixed-source arrow model. The statement specifies the containing-universe inclusion and strict enriched evaluation on all coherent mapping simplices, a projectively bifibrant universal diagram evaluating to identity, its actual ordinary covariant-unstraightening comparison over spaces, projectively bifibrant replacements after every restriction, and the exact composition law for pulled-back comparisons.
